chunks: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Hashimi, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ziyad ibn Abi Salama, who said:
I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'O Ziyad, you are working the work of the Sultan.'
I said, 'Yes.' He said to me, 'And why?' I said, 'I am a man with magnanimity, and upon me are dependents, and there is nothing behind my back (no wealth).'

He said to me, 'O Ziyad! That I should fall from a high place and be cut into piece after piece is more beloved to me than that I should govern for any one of them as an office-bearer, or roll out a carpet for one of them, except for that which I will mention.'
I said, 'I do not know, may I be sacrificed for you.'
He said, 'Except for relieving the suffering of a Believer, or freeing his chains, or paying off his debt.'
O Ziyad! The easiest of what Allah does to the one who governs for them is that a pavilion of fire is set up over him until Allah finishes the reckoning of the creatures.
O Ziyad! So if you are given charge of any of their affairs, do good to your brethren, one for one, and Allah is behind that.
O Ziyad! Whichever man from you governs for any one of them, then treats equally between you and them, say to him: 'You are an impersonating liar.'

O Ziyad! When you remember your power over the people, remember the power of Allah over you tomorrow, and the depletion of what you gave to them from them, and the remaining of what you gave to them upon you.

key_terms.سُرَادِقٌ مِنْ نَارٍ: Pavilion of fire (a specific form of punishment)
key_terms.عَمَلَ السُّلْطَانِ: Work of the Sultan (serving in the ruling government)
key_terms.فَكِّ أَسْرِهِ: Freeing his chains (from debt or captivity)
key_terms.مُنْتَحِلٌ كَذَّابٌ: Impersonating liar (claiming to be one of them but not truly)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence for a Shia official serving in a non-Shia government according to Imam Musa al-Kazim?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) cautions Ziyad ibn Abi Salama against the spiritual peril of holding public office (*amal al-sultan*) for worldly gain, emphasizing that even just administration is insufficient if not rooted in sincere service to the people. The Imam highlights that the primary justification for accepting authority is to relieve the burdens of believers—such as paying debts or freeing captives—warning that the easiest divine punishment for officials is a pavilion of fire until the Day of Judgment. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that political authority is a trust (*amanah*) requiring humility, as one must remember Allah’s power over them outweighs their power over the people.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan Al Hashimy, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ziyad Bin Abu Salma who said,
‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Ziyad! You are working as an office-bearer of the Sultan (ruling authority)?’
I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘And why?’ I said, ‘I am a man with magnanimity for me, and upon me are dependents, and there is nothing upon my back (no wealth)’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Ziyad! If I<sup>asws</sup> were to fall down from a high mountain and be cut into pieces and pieces, it would be more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than I<sup>asws</sup> govern for anyone from them as an office-bearer, or roll out a carpet for one of them, except for that’
I said, ‘I do not understand, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Except for relieving the suffering of a Believer, or freeing his chains, or paying off his debts.

O Ziyad! The easiest of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Deal with the one who rules for them as an office-bearer is that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Set up over them pavilions of Fire until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Free from Reckoning the creatures.
O Ziyad! So if you were to govern anything from their works, so reckon to your brethren, one with one (equal terms), and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is from behind that (Backer).
O Ziyad! Whichever man from you governs for anyone from them (government), so he treats equally between you and them, so say to him, ‘You are an impersonating liar’.

O Ziyad! When you remember your power over the people so remember the Power of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon you tomorrow, and it will deplete what you give to them from them (government), and it would remain upon you what you give to them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn al-Hassan al-Hashimiy has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ziyad ibn abu Salmah who has said the following:
“I once went to visit abu al-Hassan Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he (the Imam) asked me, ‘O Ziyad, do you work for Sultan ?
5 I replied, ‘Yes, I do so . 5 He (the Imam) said to me, ‘Why do you do so ? 5 I replied, ‘I am a man of fairness and I have a family to feed. I do not have any other means for support . 5

He (the Imam) said, ‘O Ziyad, if I fall from the top of a mountain and I am cut into pieces, it is more beloved to me than working for any of these people, or spread the furnishing of any of them except for what ?
5 I replied, ‘I do not know, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause . 5
He (the Imam) said, ‘Except for relieving the agony of a believer, freeing him from his shakle, or paying his debts.
O Ziyad, the least that Allah will do to those who become agents of these people for a certain work is that He will place them in the chamber of fire until Allah completes His judging all creatures.
O Ziyad, if you become the person in charge of a certain work for them, you must do good to your brothers in belief one for one and Allah is behind it (to keep the account).
O Ziyad, if anyone of you becomes the person in charge of a certain work for these people, then treats you just as he treats them, you must tell him that he is a pretending liar.

O Ziyad, if you find yourself to have power over people, you must also remember the power of Allah over you tomorrow, and that what you give them will soon perish and what you receive remains forever . 555
